meta.summary: The HAZOP of node 'MCFC stack' produced 25 scenarios, all checked against the P&ID. Flow deviations cover the Air inlet (LCV-200/FIT-110: no, less and more), the Feed inlet (LCV-100/FIT-100: no and more flow, low steam-to-carbon ratio, sulphur contamination, liquid water carry-over) and the H2 BOG inlet (LCV-300/FIT-120: less and more). Stack temperature was covered for high (electrolyte loss, seal failure, fire) and low (electrolyte freezing, matrix cracking). Pressure scenarios are a blocked outlet from spurious closure of BV-400/BV-410 (SI 5, SIL 2) and anode-cathode differential pressure. Other flow scenarios are vent release through BV-160/PSV-160, reverse flow at the outlets and inlets, and external stack leaks into the enclosure (SI 5, SIL 2). DC power deviations are overload, loss of propulsion power, reverse current and cell voltage deviation (VZA-100/110, IIC-400). The remaining scenarios are low cathode CO2, fuel admitted before the stack is purged at start-up, and loss of instrument air or control power. Main recommendations: independent trips for high-high stack temperature, low air flow and high pressure that isolate fuel through LCV-100/LCV-300; a new stack pressure transmitter and an anode-cathode differential pressure transmitter; H2/CO gas detection and ventilation of the enclosure; verifying the PSV-160 sizing, the fail positions of the LCVs and the vent location; non-return valves; a separate water/NG ratio measurement; start-up permissives with an inert purge; and reverse-current protection plus load limiting on the DC output.
meta.criteria: Default 5x5 risk ranking (FI / SI / RI / SIL)

system:
You are carrying out a HAZOP study of one node of a process plant, as an experienced process safety practitioner would.

Use the tools to work through the node:
- view_pid shows the P&ID drawing; get_node_description gives the node scope and design intent.
- list_guidewords gives the standard guidewords and parameters. Choose the deviations that are meaningful for this node.
- For each deviation, record every credible scenario with add_row: one row per cause -> consequence pair.
  Name equipment and instruments as they appear on the drawing. List existing safeguards separately from new recommendations.
- add_row checks each row and tells you if something must be fixed.
- Call finish when the node has been covered.

Risk ranking scales:
Frequency index (FI):
  5 Frequent: about once a year or more at one installation (F > 1/yr)
  4 Occasional: once in 1-10 years at one installation (1/10 yr < F < 1/yr)
  3 Rare: once in 10-100 years at one installation (1/100 yr < F < 1/10 yr)
  2 Remote: once in 100-1000 years at one installation (1/1000 yr < F < 1/100 yr)
  1 Improbable: not expected to occur (F < 1/1000 yr)
Severity index (SI):
  5 Catastrophic: multiple fatalities; uncontrolled environmental impact; loss up to about 200 MUSD
  4 Major: single fatality or multiple severe injuries; severe environmental impact; loss up to about 20 MUSD
  3 Moderate: multiple or severe injuries; major environmental impact; loss up to about 2 MUSD
  2 Significant: single or minor injury; detectable environmental impact; loss up to about 200 kUSD
  1 Minor: no injury; negligible environmental impact; loss up to about 20 kUSD
Risk index: RI = FI x SI.
Target SIL (rows SI, columns FI 1..5; 0 = no SIL requirement):
  SI 5: 1 1 2 3 3
  SI 4: 0 1 1 2 2
  SI 3: 0 0 1 1 2
  SI 2: 0 0 0 1 1
  SI 1: 0 0 0 0 0
Convention: FI and SI describe the scenario BEFORE credit is taken for the listed safeguards (unmitigated), so that the ratings can be compared with a reference worksheet that uses the same convention.

steps.text: Starting by gathering the node scope, P&ID and guidewords.

tool_calls.name: get_node_description
tool_calls.result:
{"node": "MCFC stack", "description": "Scope: the stack section of a molten carbonate fuel cell (MCFC) plant that supplies electric propulsion power on a liquefied-hydrogen carrier. The node starts at the three inlet streams (air; natural gas mixed with water, called "feed"; hydrogen boil-off gas), passes through the internal reformer, the anode and the cathode, and ends at the cathode, anode and vent outlets and at the DC power output. The drawing shows all stack modules as one segment.

Design intent and key facts:
- The stack runs at about 650 °C with a molten carbonate salt as the electrolyte.
- The feed is reformed inside the stack (steam methane reforming and water-gas shift) into H2, CO and CO2.
- At the anode, H2 and CO react with carbonate ions and release electrons; at the cathode, O2 and CO2 take up the electrons and form carbonate ions again.
- The cell reaction gives off heat; the endothermic reforming reaction is what keeps the stack in heat balance.
- The wider plant has many stack modules plus compressors for air, hydrogen and natural gas, a water pump and several heat exchangers.
- A basic process control system (BPCS) controls cell voltage and its deviation, stack and exhaust temperature, current, air flow and pressure, and fuel flow, pressure and temperature. Control and monitoring follow classification society rules."}

tool_calls.result: {"guidewords": [{"name": "No", "meaning": "Complete negation of the design intent"}, {"name": "More", "meaning": "Quantitative increase"}, {"name": "Less", "meaning": "Quantitative decrease"}, {"name": "As well as", "meaning": "Qualitative modification / addition"}, {"name": "Part of", "meaning": "Qualitative modification / decrease"}, {"name": "Reverse", "meaning": "Logical opposite of the design intent"}, {"name": "Other than", "meaning": "Complete substitution"}, {"name": "Early", "meaning": "Relative to clock time"}, {"name": "Late", "meaning": "Relative to clock time"}, {"name": "Before", "meaning": "Relating to order or sequence"}, {"name": "After", "meaning": "Relating to order or sequence"}], "parameters": ["Flow", "Pressure", "Temperature", "Level", "Composition", "Phase", "Reaction", "Power", "Mixing", "Time", "Utility", "Operation"], "deviation_format": "<Guideword> <Parameter> | <stream, line or equipment>", "source": "Guidewords follow IEC 61882:2016 (Hazard and operability studies - Application guide). The parameter list and the synonyms are a practical selection for process plants and are not part of the standard."}

steps.text: I've reviewed the P&ID. It shows the Air, Feed and H2 BOG inlets with PIT/TE/FIT-110/100/120 and LCV-200/100/300, the cathode outlet with TE/TI-310 and BV-410 (fail closed), the anode outlet with TE/TI-300 and BV-400 (fail closed), and the vent with BV-160 (fail open) and PSV-160. The DC output is monitored by VE/VZA-100 and 110, IE/II/IR-300 and IT-400. Stack temperature is measured by TE/TI-200 and 210 into TT-410, and IIC-400 adjusts LCV-100/200/300. Recording the worksheet now.

input.deviation: No Flow | Air inlet to cathode
input.causes: Air compressor trip or LCV-200 fails closed (actuator/signal fault from IIC-400)
input.consequences: No O2/CO2 to cathode; cell voltage collapses and cells reverse; Ni anode/cathode damage. Unreacted fuel leaves via the anode outlet, and propulsion power is lost.
safeguards: BPCS air flow control via IIC-400/LCV-200
recommendations: Provide low-low air flow (FIT-110) trip that isolates fuel via LCV-100/LCV-300 and initiates controlled stack shutdown, independent of BPCS

input.deviation: Less Flow | Air inlet to cathode
input.causes: Partial blockage of the air filter/line, LCV-200 throttled by a control fault, or compressor degradation
input.consequences: Cathode air is the main stack coolant, so the stack overheats with local hot spots above 700 °C. This causes electrolyte evaporation/loss, corrosion and wet-seal damage, shortens stack life and could lead to gas leakage.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210 with TT-410 stack temperature indication
recommendations: Add low air flow alarm on FIT-110 and high stack temperature alarm on TT-410

input.deviation: More Flow | Air inlet to cathode
input.causes: LCV-200 fails open or IIC-400 control fault
input.consequences: Stack is over-cooled and large thermal gradients develop. If the temperature falls below about 490 °C the carbonate electrolyte freezes and the matrix cracks, leading to gas crossover and permanent stack damage.
safeguards: BPCS temperature and air flow control
recommendations: Add low stack temperature alarm and high air flow alarm with automatic air flow limitation

input.deviation: No Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
input.causes: NG compressor or water pump trip, or LCV-100 fails closed
input.consequences: Anode is starved of H2/CO and the Ni anode oxidises, causing voltage collapse and loss of power. If H2 BOG continues, the endothermic reforming heat sink is lost and the stack overheats.
recommendations: Interlock low feed flow (FIT-100) to reduce DC load via IIC-400 and limit H2 BOG via LCV-300

input.deviation: More Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
input.causes: LCV-100 fails open or flow control fault
input.consequences: Excess endothermic reforming cools the stack locally (risk of electrolyte freezing at the inlet). Excess unreacted CH4/H2 goes to the anode outlet and downstream, and fuel is wasted.
recommendations: Add high feed flow alarm on FIT-100

input.deviation: Less Composition | Feed steam-to-carbon ratio
input.causes: Water pump failure/low water flow while NG flow continues (FIT-100 measures only total feed)
input.consequences: Carbon is deposited on the reformer catalyst and anode. This blocks gas channels, raises pressure drop, deactivates the catalyst and causes irreversible stack damage.
recommendations: Provide separate NG and water flow measurement with a low steam-to-carbon ratio alarm and trip of NG supply

input.deviation: Other than Composition | Feed (sulphur/contaminants in natural gas)
input.causes: Desulphurisation upstream fails or is saturated, or the NG supply is off-spec
input.consequences: Sulphur poisons the reformer catalyst and Ni anode, causing progressive voltage loss and stack degradation.
recommendations: Provide sulphur breakthrough monitoring/periodic analysis downstream of the desulphuriser

input.deviation: Other than Phase | Feed (liquid water carry-over)
input.causes: Upstream vaporiser/heat exchanger failure lets liquid water reach the stack inlet
input.consequences: Liquid water hits the 650 °C reformer, causing thermal shock, cracking of catalyst/plates and local quenching of cells.
recommendations: Add low feed temperature alarm/trip on TE-100 to close LCV-100

input.deviation: Less Flow | H2 BOG to anode
input.causes: BOG compressor trip, low boil-off rate or LCV-300 fails closed
input.consequences: Fuel to the anode drops and fuel utilisation rises. Power output falls, the propulsion load cannot be met, and the anode is at risk of local fuel starvation.

input.deviation: More Flow | H2 BOG to anode
input.causes: LCV-300 fails open, IIC-400 fault, or BOG surge from the cargo tanks
input.consequences: Excess H2 oxidation without the matching endothermic reforming leads to stack overheating. Excess unburnt H2 goes to the anode outlet, creating a flammable atmosphere downstream.
recommendations: Provide high H2 BOG flow alarm and high-high stack temperature trip closing LCV-300 (independent of BPCS)

input.deviation: More Temperature | Stack (anode/cathode)
input.causes: BPCS temperature control failure, TE-200/TE-210 reading falsely low, loss of reforming heat sink, high current or low cathode air
input.consequences: Above about 700 °C the electrolyte evaporates and wet seals fail. Hot H2/CO can leak into the enclosure with fire/explosion risk and severe stack damage.
recommendations: Implement SIL 1 high-high stack temperature trip (voted TE-200/TE-210) closing LCV-100/LCV-300 and reducing load
Provide TE deviation alarm between TE-200 and TE-210

input.deviation: Less Temperature | Stack (anode/cathode)
input.causes: Excess air or feed flow, prolonged low load/idle, or low inlet temperatures (TE-100/110/120)
input.consequences: Carbonate electrolyte solidifies and the matrix cracks, causing gas crossover between anode and cathode and permanent stack loss.
recommendations: Add low stack temperature alarm with automatic load/air adjustment and a hot-standby heating procedure

input.deviation: More Pressure | Stack (blocked outlet)
input.causes: BV-400 or BV-410 closes spuriously (fail-closed on signal/air loss) while inlet flows continue
input.consequences: Stack overpressure causes wet-seal blow-out, anode/cathode gas crossover and mixing of H2/CO with air at 650 °C. This can cause internal combustion, fire or explosion and release from the stack.
recommendations: Interlock closure of BV-400/BV-410 to close LCV-100/LCV-200/LCV-300 and open BV-160
Add stack pressure transmitter with high-high pressure trip (SIL 2 assessment)
Verify PSV-160 sizing for blocked-outlet case

input.deviation: Other than Pressure | Anode-cathode differential pressure
input.causes: Imbalance between air control (LCV-200) and fuel control (LCV-100/LCV-300), or sudden loss of air pressure
input.consequences: Wet seal/electrolyte matrix breakthrough lets fuel cross into the cathode (or air into the anode). This causes direct combustion, hot spots, stack fire and permanent damage.
safeguards: PIT-110, PIT-100, PIT-120 inlet pressure indication
recommendations: Install anode-cathode differential pressure transmitter with alarm and trip

input.deviation: More Flow | Vent line (BV-160 / PSV-160)
input.causes: BV-160 opens spuriously (fail open on signal/air loss), or PSV-160 lifts/passes
input.consequences: Hot H2/CO-rich gas is released to Vent Out, forming a flammable/toxic cloud on deck with possible ignition, and stack pressure is lost.
safeguards: Vent Out routed outside the skid
recommendations: Confirm vent outlet is located in a safe area per class rules, with dispersion study
Add position indication/alarm on BV-160

input.deviation: Reverse Flow | Anode Out / Cathode Out
input.causes: Stack pressure drops during shutdown/trip while the downstream header remains pressurised, or BV-400/BV-410 is passing
input.consequences: Air/exhaust enters the anode, oxidising the Ni anode. A flammable mixture may form inside the stack.
recommendations: Install non-return valves on anode and cathode outlets
Provide inert gas purge on shutdown

input.deviation: Reverse Flow | Air / Feed / H2 BOG inlets
input.causes: Loss of upstream compressor/supply pressure while the stack is still pressurised
input.consequences: Hot fuel gas flows back into the air line (or air into the fuel lines), forming a flammable mixture upstream with fire/explosion risk.
recommendations: Install non-return valves upstream of LCV-100, LCV-200 and LCV-300
Low inlet pressure trip closing the respective LCV

input.deviation: Other than Flow | Stack external leak
input.causes: Wet seal degradation, corrosion, thermal cycling or ship motion/vibration
input.consequences: H2/CO released into the fuel cell room causes fire/explosion and toxic CO exposure to crew.
recommendations: Provide H2 and CO gas detection in the stack enclosure with ESD isolating LCV-100/LCV-300
Provide mechanical ventilation of the enclosure with monitoring per class rules

input.deviation: More Power | DC-Power output
input.causes: Propulsion overload demand, short circuit downstream, or IIC-400 current control fault
input.consequences: High current means high fuel utilisation, causing fuel starvation, cell reversal, local overheating and anode oxidation.
recommendations: Provide overcurrent protection and load-limiting by power management system
Interlock current limit to available fuel flow (FIT-100/FIT-120)

input.deviation: No Power | DC-Power output
input.causes: Load disconnection/breaker trip, or stack trip
input.consequences: The vessel loses propulsion, with risk of collision/grounding. At open circuit the cell voltage is high, no reaction heat is produced, unreacted fuel goes to the anode outlet and the stack cools.
recommendations: Ensure power management reduces fuel automatically on load loss
Verify redundancy of propulsion power (other modules/battery) per class requirements

input.deviation: Reverse Power | DC-Power output
input.causes: Back-feed from battery/other parallel modules into a weak or tripped stack
input.consequences: Cells are driven in reverse (electrolysis), causing anode/cathode corrosion and stack damage.
recommendations: Provide blocking diode/reverse current protection on DC output

input.deviation: Other than Power | Cell voltage deviation
input.causes: Individual cell degradation, local fuel starvation or flow maldistribution
input.consequences: Weak cells reverse, causing local hot spots, electrolyte loss and possible seal failure leading to a gas leak.
recommendations: Provide automatic load reduction on high cell voltage deviation

input.deviation: Less Composition | CO2 at cathode
input.causes: High share of H2 BOG relative to natural gas feed (little CO2 in anode exhaust recycled to cathode)
input.consequences: Carbonate ions are not regenerated, so electrolyte is depleted, cell voltage drops and performance degrades.
recommendations: Define minimum NG/BOG ratio in control philosophy, or CO2 make-up

input.deviation: Before Operation | Start-up fuel admission
input.causes: Fuel (LCV-100/LCV-300) admitted before the stack is purged and heated, due to operator error or sequence fault
input.consequences: Residual air and fuel form a flammable mixture inside the hot stack, leading to internal explosion and stack destruction.
recommendations: Implement start-up permissives (purge complete, stack temperature) on LCV-100/LCV-300
Provide inert gas purge system and written start-up procedure

input.deviation: No Utility | Instrument air / control power
input.causes: Loss of instrument air or control power to the valves
input.consequences: BV-400 and BV-410 close and BV-160 opens. If LCV-100/LCV-200/LCV-300 do not fail closed, fuel continues into the stack and is vented through Vent Out, giving a flammable release, possible overpressure and loss of propulsion.
recommendations: Define and verify fail-closed position of LCV-100 and LCV-300 (fuel) and appropriate fail position of LCV-200
Provide UPS for BPCS and stack monitoring

steps.text: I've now checked the P&ID image and it matches the tags used in rows 1–25: PIT/TE/FIT-110/100/120 with LCV-200/100/300; TE/TI-310 and BV-410 (FC) on Cathode Out; TE/TI-300 and BV-400 (FC) on Anode Out; BV-160 (FO) and PSV-160 to Vent Out; VE/VZA-100 (low alarm) and VE/VZA-110 (high alarm); IE/II/IR-300 and IT-400; TE/TI-200 and 210 into TT-410 and on to IIC-400, which drives LCV-100/200/300. There is an anode-to-cathode transfer inside the stack, so row 23 is consistent too. I also checked every SIL value against the matrix. No corrections are needed, so I'm finishing the node.
